title: Trump dodged Yemen's plea for military support amid Houthi attacks on Riyadh: Report
content: President Trump did not commit US forces to aid Yemen against the Houthis.  Yemeni President Alimi sought American backing for his government's efforts.  US officials met Houthi representatives in Oman, discussing a ceasefire.  Trump reportedly called off planned airstrikes against Houthi targets.  The conflict has caused significant casualties and displacement within Yemen.

title: Ishan is the 'chosen one'? Mayawati's latest U-turn deepens ongoing BSP family drama
content: In a strategic move, Mayawati has selected Ishan Anand for an important party role, succeeding his brother Akash Anand who was recently ousted. Akash's conduct and the potential influence of his father-in-law were cited as reasons for this decision. Mayawati highlights the necessity of integrity and commitment for Ishan as he embarks on this new chapter in the BSP.

title: Pak in crisis: PTI to hold Sept 27 stir 'at all costs' for release of Imran Khan
content: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf plans a protest on September 27 for Imran Khan's release. Legal challenges have been filed against the detention of his three sisters. The party insists the demonstrations will proceed despite arrests of its leaders. Authorities state the protest will not be allowed to disrupt the capital city. Imran Khan's son condemned the detentions and called for international intervention.

title: USCIS warns against websites and businesses ‘guaranteeing’ faster visa
content: USCIS warns applicants about businesses falsely promising faster visa and Green Card processing. These entities claim special government connections and demand fees for expedited services. Applicants should use official .gov resources and report suspicious offers to avoid unauthorized providers. The Department of Justice offers lists of low-cost or free legal immigration services. USCIS also provides tips for accurately completing and submitting application forms online.

title: Retired man deposits Rs 1.33cr, files no ITR; taxman sends notice, what ITAT said
content: The Income Tax Department also noted that the individuals had not filed an income tax return (ITR) for the relevant year. This meant the department did not have details of the income he had earned during the period under scrutiny.

title: Oilers linked to Dylan Larkin trade in Matthew Savoie-led blockbuster
content: The Edmonton Oilers are speculated to be considering a trade that would bring Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin into their lineup. Reports suggest a trade package featuring Matthew Savoie along with other young prospects. However, Larkin’s contract complications and his no-trade clause could hinder any discussions. With Detroit's focus on a non-rebuilding strategy, this remains more of a theoretical scenario than a likely transaction.

title: 84-year-old veteran donated 207-acre llama ranch; now it is a sanctuary
content: In an inspiring act of philanthropy, Navy veteran Al Ellis has gifted his expansive ranch in Wyoming to a dedicated foundation. This sanctuary will cater to veterans and first responders, providing a serene environment for healing and family bonding. With the Boulder Crest Foundation’s specialized initiatives, the campus is anticipated to be operational by September 2027, transforming lives one family at a time.

title: Pink bought 200-acre California ranch; 13 years later, it became a vineyard
content: Pink bought a 200-acre California ranch with her husband Carey Hart for nearly $9 million in 2013. What began as an interest in wine grew into Two Wolves, an organic wine business. After years of studying winemaking and making small batches privately, Pink released her first vintage in 2014 and has since built a team around organic farming and winemaking.

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.

title: New Jersey man’s free lawn-mowing network grows to 2,000 volunteers across US
content: In 2020, New Jersey resident Brian Schwartz lost his job during the pandemic and began mowing lawns for free to help older neighbours. That one‑off act grew into I Want To Mow Your Lawn, a volunteer‑run nonprofit now linking more than 2,000 volunteers in all 50 states with seniors, veterans and others who need temporary yard help.

title: Manoj Bajpayee moves Delhi High Court to protect personality rights from AI misuse
content: In a notable legal move, actor Manoj Bajpayee has turned to the Delhi High Court to safeguard his identity. He claims his image and voice have been used without permission, particularly through AI technologies. The court raised issues regarding jurisdiction; however, Bajpayee's legal team referenced defendants based in Delhi. This petition mirrors the growing trend of public figures seeking similar protections due to concerns over unauthorized endorsements and AI-generated content.

title: The 'rebel' hit by rebellion: How Mamata's TMC journey has come full circle
content: Nearly three decades after Mamata Banerjee broke away from the Congress to build the Trinamool Congress, she finds herself in a very different battle: fighting a rebellion within her own party, a dispute over its name and symbol, and a stronger BJP in Bengal has pushed back to the 'sister party'.

title: Naomi Osaka’s family faced eviction: How did she rise to Grand Slam glory?
content: During the evolution of her remarkable tennis career, which boasts four Grand Slam titles and a peak world ranking of number one, Naomi Osaka navigated challenging eviction notices. Beyond her athletic achievements, she has ventured into investments and sports ownership, notably launching successful skincare and media companies. Currently, she is ambitiously embracing luxury fashion projects, showcasing her versatility beyond the tennis court.

title: Rhea Ripley’s journey: How did she become one of WWE’s biggest stars?
content: Rhea Ripley’s path from the independent wrestling scene in Australia to a successful career in the WWE, winning big gold titles, developing her character and appearing in high-profile WrestleMania matches. Ripley trained at Riot City Wrestling before working her way through NXT UK and NXT to the main WWE roster. Her transformation into “Mami” and involvement in The Judgement Day also raised her profile globally.

title: Jordon Hudson and Bill Belichick: How did their relationship begin?
content: Bill Belichick rarely discusses his personal life, making his comments about Jordon Hudson particularly notable. During a 2025 interview, he praised Hudson as “terrific” and “very helpful,” explaining that she supported him with business matters and his book while he focused on coaching at North Carolina. His remarks offered a glimpse into their relationship, emphasizing companionship, trust, support, and mutual perspective.

title: Monty Python star says he wants to be buried in Provence after surviving cancer
content: Monty Python star Eric Idle, 83, has opened up about surviving pancreatic cancer, his peaceful life in Provence and his views on mortality. Idle also recalled a 2001 conversation with Beatles legend George Harrison about death and rebirth, revealing their differing beliefs about the afterlife during Harrison’s final days and his iconic comedy legacy.

title: UK to introduce special rape and serious sexual offence courts, amid low prosecution rate
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced dedicated courts for sexual offence cases. These new courts aim to expedite convictions and reduce case backlogs significantly.  Specialized training will be provided to court personnel for handling sensitive cases.  Victims will receive a dedicated point of contact throughout the legal process.  This initiative supports the government's commitment to reducing violence against women.

title: ‘Resolve issues through dialogue’: Govt urges bank employees to call off Sept 28-30 stir
content: The finance ministry urged bank employees to resolve demands through dialogue.  A three-day nationwide strike is planned from September 28 to 30.  Unions seek a five-day banking week and withdrawal of the PLI scheme.  The government has addressed most concerns and is examining remaining issues.  Banks are preparing for potential disruptions and advising customers to use digital services.

title: Chess Olympiad forfeit row: Israel blasts FIDE for not honouring 'commitments'
content: Israel Chess Federation chief Zvika Barkai has accused FIDE of failing to honour a prior agreement over scheduling Israel’s Chess Olympiad matches around Yom Kippur. Both Israeli teams forfeited their Round 6 games after the Netherlands and Bulgaria declined schedule changes. Barkai praised Singapore and Colombia for accommodating Israel, criticised FIDE’s handling, and warned the forfeits could significantly affect Israel’s rankings.

title: 'Dhoni calling the shots': How Zaheer pipped Hemang Badani for CSK head coach job
content: Zaheer Khan has emerged as Chennai Super Kings' surprise choice to replace Stephen Fleming after talks with front-runner Hemang Badani broke down over contract length and the franchise's limited portfolio.

title: Why world No.1 Sinner cannot afford to skip the Asian swing despite his injury
content: Jannik Sinner faces a key comeback decision after missing the US Open with a knee issue. He could return in Beijing and Shanghai, where heat and humidity have previously troubled him, or wait until Vienna. Delaying his return could protect his fitness but give Alexander Zverev a chance to reduce his ranking deficit before the ATP Finals in Turin.

title: Trump traded more securities than all Congress; backs stock-buying ban for all lawmakers

title: Asian Games Medal Tally: Where India stands after 4 more medals as China dominate

China continued to dominate Aichi-Nagoya, extending its lead at the top of the standings as the medal race takes shape.

title: Flight fare analysis: How to get cheaper tickets by booking in advance - decoded
content: A ticket bought the day before departure costs about 25% more than the same journey booked 30 days ahead. On all 54 metro routes tracked, not one is cheaper to book late. The penalty runs from 3% on Bengaluru to Chennai to 121% on Ahmedabad to Pune. Thirty days out is the floor. Booking two or three months ahead is slightly dearer than booking one.

title: Delhi jail shocker: Undertrial stabbed in neck by 2 inmates inside Rohini prison
content: An undertrial inmate was fatally stabbed by two fellow prisoners inside Delhi's Rohini Central Jail. The deceased, Pradeep alias Mohinder, sustained a neck injury from a sharp weapon. He was returning to his barrack when the alleged attack occurred on Monday. Hospital officials declared him brought dead after his swift transfer for treatment. Police are registering a case and examining CCTV footage of the incident.

title: Mamata Banerjee-led TMC camp unveils ‘football player’ as new party logo
content: Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction has unveiled a new symbol featuring the football player symbol allotted to it by the Election Commission for the October 6 bypolls. The move comes after the EC froze the party’s familiar name and flowers-and-grass symbol amid the internal dispute over control of the TMC. With the Supreme Court set to hear Banerjee’s challenge to the EC order, the faction is racing to familiarise voters with its new identity ahead of the polls.

title: Teenage shuttler first athlete suspended after positive dope test at Asian Games 2026
content: Teenage badminton sensation Pitchamon Opatniputh from Thailand is facing a provisional suspension in light of testing positive for furosemide, a banned diuretic. This incident marks the first provisional suspension related to the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Games, sidestepping the athlete’s chance to compete or even train. The next steps will unfold to reveal the final decision regarding this anti-doping matter.

title: Caught on camera: Speeding Thar rams into scooter, 57-year-old dies
content:
The deceased was identified as Naval Sharma (Visuals-Social Media)

JAIPUR: A 57-year-old dairy operator was killed after his scooter was allegedly hit from behind by a speeding SUV in Jaipur's Sanganer area, police said on Monday. The accident took place on Saturday morning, while CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Monday, police said. The deceased was identified as Naval Sharma, a resident of Buddhsinghpura in Sanganer. According to police, Sharma had left his home on his scooter around 6 am on Saturday to go to his dairy when a Mahindra Thar allegedly hit him from behind. The driver fled the spot after the accident, they said. Passersby informed the police, following which Sharma was taken to a hospital. He succumbed to his injuries during treatment. His body was handed over to his family on Sunday afternoon after a post-mortem examination at SMS Hospital. Police have formed two teams to trace the unidentified vehicle and arrest its driver.(With Agency Inputs)
